# Gevurah Critique — Do Not Trade Proof for Speed

The Awtsmoos can reveal speed without confusion; Awtsmoos.com must reject any optimization that makes frame identity, timing, or failure propagation obscure.

1. The sequential path has already survived 360 real frames and native finalization.
2. Parallel canvases multiply renderer memory and may contend on one browser main thread, producing little gain.
3. `CanvasMovieRenderer.render()` appears synchronous; multiple JS promises do not make synchronous Canvas drawing parallel on the main thread.
4. `canvas.toBlob()` is asynchronous and may benefit from overlap, but drawing for another frame must not mutate the same canvas while encoding.
5. Independent canvases solve mutation risk but increase memory and DOM work.
6. Out-of-order frame uploads are safe only because server filenames are explicit integer indices and finalization verifies exact count.
7. Progress must count acknowledged unique frame indices, not launched work.
8. Any lane failure must reject the entire pump and prevent finalize.
9. A new parallel path needs source, tests, benchmark, reread, and full gate before the 180-second render can start.
10. That verification overhead could cost more than simply running the proven sequential baseline.
11. The current machine is under significant shared tunnel/browser load, so aggressive parallelism may hurt total throughput.
12. The completion requirement values verified output over minimum wall time.

## Decision pressure
Because the short proof already demonstrates correctness and because Canvas rendering remains main-thread synchronous, the safest choice is to launch the proven sequential full render now rather than introduce a fresh concurrency subsystem at the decisive evidence gate. Use sparse polling and perform non-browser shadow work while it runs.
